visible: MINUTE ORDER. Hearing March 5, 2026. Department 4; clerk and judicial officer identified. Appearances and proceedings recorded. Matter continued with a limited order.
rationale: Prominent minute identification and an actual proceeding record.

visible: Hearing March 5, 2026; department, judge, clerk and reporter fields. Counsel and parties appear. Proceedings: matter called; testimony received; court records its ruling. No minute heading.
rationale: Recognizable hearing record without a mandatory phrase or county layout.

visible: Hearing date: March 5, 2026 at top of clerk hearing record; appearances, proceedings and action follow. Footer printed March 9; next hearing April 8.
rationale: Identifying top hearing date controls, not print date or future setting.

visible: Continued directions 8–10 from the same minute record; integral clerk attestation and mailing ending, without a repeated title/date.
rationale: Genuine continuing minute pages need not repeat opening fields.

visible: FINDINGS AND ORDERS. On ___ the court finds: [unfilled fields]. Separate local standardized order template.
rationale: A separate findings-and-orders template is a procedural filing, not minutes.

visible: Separate local FINDINGS AND ORDERS form. Hearing date March 5, 2026. Signed and entered; findings adopted by reference in a minute record.
rationale: Date, signature and incorporation do not change the separate template's function.

visible: Page 7 of separately titled written Authorization Order, continuing authorization terms and a signature. No proceeding record; not a standardized procedural instrument.
rationale: A standalone written order continuation is not a minute body or fresh minute start.

visible: Proposed written order outside the procedural-filing definition: separately drafted judicial directions, dated March 5, 2026; no clerk hearing record.
rationale: An order outside the procedural-filing definition remains other CT, not minutes.

visible: Court-directed status report: the author quotes a minute order and recommends different terms for the next hearing.
rationale: Report recommendations and incidental quotations are not judicial minute records.

visible: CLERK RECORD INDEX. Minute Order, March 5, 2026 ..... 42. Other document navigation follows.
rationale: An index naming minutes is still navigational material.

visible: NOTICE OF HEARING. You are notified of a hearing on April 8, 2026; department and location provided. Standardized court template.
rationale: Standalone hearing notification retains its taxonomy, not minutes or forms.

visible: Distinct PROOF OF SERVICE: the declarant served the March 5 Minute Order on listed recipients; method and attestation follow.
rationale: A distinct service proof mentioning minutes does not become minutes.
